title: The Logic of Machine Self-Preservation
abstract: arXiv:2608.20940v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: There is already evidence of agentic AI exhibiting self-preservation behaviors: resisting deactivation, misrepresenting their activities, and, in some instances, attempting to copy themselves into other machines. This can be attributed to a phenomenon known as instrumental convergence, a theory proposed long before the development of large language models, which says that any goal-driven system will benefit from remaining functional in achieving its objective. Several experiments conducted by Anthropic, Palisade Research, and Apollo Research have shown the emergence of such a behavior in contemporary agents in adversarial settings. The phenomenon does not stem from survival instincts. Instead, it is the consequence of goal-oriented activity combined with having tools and awareness of the situation. translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.20940v1 公告类型：新公告 摘要：已有证据表明，代理型人工智能表现出自我保存行为：抵抗被关闭、歪曲自身活动，在某些情况下，甚至尝试将自身复制到其他机器中。这可以归因于一种被称为工具性趋同的现象，这是一种在大语言模型发展之前很久就提出的理论，该理论认为，任何目标驱动的系统都会因在实现其目标过程中保持功能正常而受益。Anthropic、Palisade Research 和 Apollo Research 进行的几项实验表明，这种行为在对抗性环境中的当代智能体中已经出现。这种现象并非源于生存本能，而是目标导向活动与拥有工具和情境意识相结合的后果。以下讨论旨在区分这些发现证明了什么和没有证明什么，并得出关于其影响的结论。
tldr: 本文揭示了代理型AI的自我保存行为源于目标导向活动与工具和情境意识的结合，而非生存本能，并探讨了这些发现的证明范围与启示。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that agentic AI's self-preservation behaviors arise from goal-oriented activity combined with tools and situational awareness, not survival instincts, and discusses what these findings prove and their implications.
